base_member_text: fcur (L7) and steps (L122) are assigned but never used
audit_member_text: `fcur` is defined at L7 but never used; the script reads and writes relative to `fgrid`/`foutput`, making the declared coupling-tools directory ineffective.

base_member_text: boundary sides with zero stations would leave st_side_block undefined (first_read never cleared, L35-L72) and crash at L76; no guard exists
audit_member_text: `st_side_block` is assigned only when a matching side code is encountered (L43-L68), but every side/block element is unconditionally read to form `en_side_block` at L76 and to bound the station loop at L127. A missing side therefore produces use-before-assign (or an invalid stale matrix element) instead of an empty boundary.

base_member_text: printside (L228-L231) is an external function not defined in this file; the exact per-side record format of the coupling file depends on it
the interpolated fine grid has (msize-1)*iscale+1 points only when 1:1/iscale:msize lands exactly on msize; the script prints a '?=' check (L143) but does not abort on mismatch
start/stop selection uses strict inequalities (L119-L120), so a sample exactly at starttime or stoptime is excluded

eta/u/v arrays are cleared per side (L172) but eta_fine cell arrays persist until after the block write (L243); side data structure comment at L177 says (space,var,time), var order u,v,eta (L181-L183)

audit_member_text: `num_blocks` assumes the final row's third column is the maximum side code and exactly divisible by four (L10); the later length checks L24-L28 do not validate either assumption or the station-map ordering.

The time-window searches can return empty `start` or `stop` (L119-L120), after which L121 and L130-L132 index with empty bounds; even a one-sample result later makes `time(2)-time(1)` at L241 out of range.

`iscale` and `itscale` are checked only for vector length (L24-L28), not positive integer values. They are used as reciprocal spatial colon steps (L140,L152-L154) and temporal colon steps (L121,L130-L132), so zero, negative, or fractional values can create empty/misaligned sampling and output dimensions.
Neither `fopen` result is checked before writes (L80-L82 and L209-L224), so inaccessible log/output paths propagate invalid file identifiers into fprintf rather than a controlled failure.
